methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json), not from medical memory. Generic structural headings (organizational section umbrellas with no independent content) are NOT converted into standalone units - see organizational_header_nodes below for how each is accounted for.

same_page_merge_resolutions.CP.S01: Same-page merge of two real printed headings ('ACFOMYMS', 'General Principles', both indexed to TN page CP2 / pdf 176) confirmed via raw OCR of the TOC page (0175.json) and body page (0176.json). Split into SU-CP-01 (Acronyms) and SU-CP-02/SU-CP-03 (General Principles, further subdivided by its own three printed sub-headings: Drug Nomenclature + Phases of Clinical Drug Testing combined into SU-CP-02; Drug Administration kept separate as SU-CP-03 given its substantially deeper table-based content).
same_page_merge_resolutions.CP.S04: Same-page merge of two real printed headings ('Adverse Drug Reactions', 'Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology', both indexed to TN page CP11 / pdf 185) confirmed via raw OCR of the TOC page (0175.json) and body pages (0185.json, 0186.json). Split into SU-CP-13 (Adverse Drug Reactions + Approach to Suspected ADRs), SU-CP-14 (Drug Interactions, kept separate given its extensive named-interaction sidebar), and SU-CP-15 (Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology, covering Parasympathetic NS + Sympathetic NS). The merge's third nested TOC sub-entry, 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain', is thematically unrelated to autonomic physiology despite its TOC indentation under that heading, and is represented separately as SU-CP-16.
same_page_merge_resolutions.CP.S06: Same-page merge of two real printed headings ('Landmark Pharmacology Trials', 'References', both indexed to TN page CP14 / pdf 188) confirmed via raw OCR of the TOC page (0175.json) and body page (0188.json). Split into SU-CP-19 (Landmark Pharmacology Trials) and SU-CP-20 (References). UNLIKE the ELOM ELOM.S04 precedent (where a 'References'-labelled node turned out to be a misattributed disclaimer paragraph, not a genuine bibliography), raw OCR of pdf page 188 confirms CP.S06's 'References' heading here genuinely IS a correctly-attributed, >30-entry chapter bibliography with no clinical/testable content mixed in -- so no content was reattached elsewhere; SU-CP-20 is retained as a pure REFERENCE_ONLY unit, matching the treatment given to the equivalent genuine References sections in Chapters A and C.

unresolved_heading_resolution: None - research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json records 0 entries for chapter_code CP (independently verified: filtering the 27 total unresolved_headings entries by chapter_code == 'CP' returns an empty list), and a sanity pass over all of CP's body pages (176-188) found no further structurally-off content beyond the three documented same-page merges above.

study_units.title: Acronyms (Chapter Glossary)
study_units.structural_rationale: Same-page-merge protocol applied to CP.S01: its merged_duplicate_headings field lists 'General Principles' as a heading absorbed into this node because both share the printed TOC page label CP2 (pdf 176). Raw OCR of the TOC page (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0175.json) confirms two separate printed TOC entries both indexed to CP2: 'ACFOMYMS . . . CP2' and 'General Principles. . . CP2' (the latter itself printing three further unindented sub-entries: Drug Nomenclature, Phases of Clinical Drug Testing, Drug Administration). Raw OCR of the body page (0176.json) confirms the printed structure exactly: the page opens with a multi-column acronym-definition table (ACE, ACh, ADE, ADME... through TI, Vd), immediately followed by a distinct bold 'General Principles' heading. This unit represents ONLY the acronym-table portion; the 'General Principles' portion (with its three sub-headings) is SU-CP-02.

study_units.title: General Principles: Drug Nomenclature and Phases of Clinical Drug Testing
source_hierarchy_path: CP.S01 (ACFOMYMS) [same-page merge resolution: General Principles portion]
study_units.structural_rationale: Second resolved heading from the CP.S01 same-page merge (see SU-CP-01). Raw OCR of body page 0176.json confirms 'General Principles' as a distinct bold heading directly beneath the acronym table, immediately followed by its own two confirmed sub-headings on the same page: 'Drug Nomenclature' (DIN/NDC/DIN-HM/NPN identifiers, chemical vs. non-proprietary/generic vs. proprietary/trade naming conventions) and 'Phases of Clinical Drug Testing' (pre-clinical through phase IV, including RCT design and post-marketing surveillance). Both are thin, definitional, orientation-level content that frame later chapter material (drug naming conventions recur throughout; trial-phase vocabulary underlies the 'Landmark Pharmacology Trials' section, SU-CP-19) rather than being independently testable clinical competencies of their own. The third sub-heading of 'General Principles', 'Drug Administration', has substantially deeper content (a full comparative table of 12+ routes) and is represented separately as SU-CP-03.

study_units.title: Drug Administration: Routes and Selection
source_hierarchy_path: CP.S01 (ACFOMYMS) [same-page merge resolution: General Principles > Drug Administration portion]
study_units.structural_rationale: Third sub-heading of 'General Principles' (see SU-CP-02). 'Drug Administration' heading confirmed at the bottom of pdf page 176 (0176.json), with its content -- Table 1, 'Routes of Drug Administration' (oral, buccal/sublingual, rectal, IV, IM, SC, intrathecal, inhalation, topical, transdermal, intraperitoneal/intra-articular, intranasal, vaginal, intraosseous), each with advantages/disadvantages -- confirmed continuing onto pdf page 177 (0177.json), ending immediately before the 'Pharmacokinetics' section heading on the same page. Represented as its own unit separate from SU-CP-02 because, unlike Nomenclature/Trial-Phases, route selection by patient context (e.g., NPO/vomiting/unconscious -> parenteral route; need for rapid onset -> IV/sublingual; avoiding first-pass -> sublingual/rectal/transdermal) is a genuine bedside decision point.

study_units.title: Pharmacokinetics Overview and Drug Absorption
source_hierarchy_path: CP.S02 (Pharmacokinetics) [thin organizational header: two definitional bullets, no further independent content]
study_units.structural_rationale: CP.S02's own heading has only two brief definitional bullets ('what the body does to the drug'; the ADME process list) confirmed on pdf page 177 (0177.json), immediately followed by the 'Absorption' heading with no other intervening content -- functionally an organizational header rather than independent testable content, so its two bullets are folded into this unit's framing rather than given a separate unit. 'Absorption' content (mechanisms of absorption, factors affecting rate/extent) is confirmed starting on pdf 177 and continuing onto pdf 178 (0178.json) with 'Bioavailability (F)', 'First-Pass Effect', and 'Drug Transporters' (P-glycoprotein substrates/inhibitors/inducers) as confirmed sub-headings, ending immediately before the 'Distribution' heading on the same page.

study_units.title: Drug Distribution (Volume of Distribution, Protein Binding, Depots, Barriers)
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Distribution' heading confirmed on pdf page 178 (0178.json): body-fluid/tissue compartments, factors affecting distribution, plasma protein binding (albumin for acidic drugs, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein for basic drugs). Content continues onto pdf 179 (0179.json) with 'Volume of Distribution' (Vd formula, small vs. large Vd interpretation, age-related changes), 'Depot' (fat as a reservoir for lipophilic drugs, IM depot formulations), and 'Barriers' (BBB, placenta), ending immediately before the 'Metabolism (Biotransformation)' heading on the same page.

study_units.title: Drug Metabolism and Cytochrome P450-Mediated Interactions
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Metabolism (Biotransformation)' heading confirmed on pdf page 179 (0179.json): sites of biotransformation, prodrug activation/toxic-metabolite examples, phase I (oxidation/reduction/hydrolysis, largely CYP-mediated) vs. phase II (conjugation) reactions, and genetic-polymorphism examples (CYP2D6 prodrug activators tamoxifen/tramadol/codeine, CYP2C9-metabolized warfarin). Content continues onto pdf 180 (0180.json) with CYP inhibition/induction mechanisms and named clinical examples (erythromycin+simvastatin, grapefruit juice+CYP3A4 substrates, carbamazepine auto-induction, phenobarbital+oral contraceptives, alcohol/smoking effects on CYP2E1/CYP1A2), plus liver/renal disease and extremes-of-age effects on biotransformation, ending immediately before the 'Excretion' heading on the same page.

study_units.title: Drug Excretion and Renal Elimination
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Excretion' heading confirmed on pdf page 180 (0180.json): renal clearance formula (glomerular filtration + tubular secretion - tubular reabsorption), age/disease effects on renal function, mechanisms of each renal process (including transporter-mediated secretion competition, e.g., probenecid inhibiting penicillin excretion), and non-renal routes (biliary/enterohepatic recirculation, pulmonary, minor routes including breast milk), ending immediately before the 'Pharmacokinetic Considerations' heading on the same page.

study_units.title: Pharmacokinetic Parameters and Dosing Strategy (Half-Life, Clearance, Steady-State, Loading/Maintenance Dosing)
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Pharmacokinetic Considerations' heading confirmed on pdf page 180 (0180.json), opening with time-course-of-drug-action framing and 'Half-Life' (definition, first-order-kinetics dependence, 4-5 half-lives to steady state). Content continues onto pdf 181 (0181.json) with 'Steady-State Drug Concentration', 'Clearance' (Cl formula, total-body clearance), 'Elimination Kinetics' (first-order vs. zero-order/non-linear, with named zero-order examples: alcohol, phenytoin, high-dose ASA), and 'Loading and Maintenance Doses', ending immediately before the 'Pharmacodynamics' heading on the same page.

study_units.title: Pharmacodynamics: Dose-Response, Efficacy, Potency, and Therapeutic Index
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Pharmacodynamics' heading confirmed opening pdf page 181 (0181.json): graded dose-response relationship, 'Efficacy' (Emax) and 'Potency' (EC50/ED50, with Figure 1's log-dose-response curve). The chapter's printed sequence then places 'Effects of Drugs on Receptors' (CP.S02.T07, confirmed pdf 182, 0182.json) between this unit's two halves; that content is thematically distinct (agonist/antagonist mechanism rather than dose-response magnitude) and is represented separately as SU-CP-10, per the same principle used to split closely-adjacent-but-distinct topics in the Cardiology/Anesthesia pilots. This unit's remaining content -- 'Effectiveness and Safety' (ED50/LD50/TD50 definitions) and 'Therapeutic Indices' (TI = TD50/ED50, narrow-TI drug list requiring TDM, Certain Safety Factor) -- is confirmed on pdf page 183 (0183.json), continuing the same dose-response-curve conceptual thread begun on pdf 181 (Figures 4-6 on pdf 183 directly extend Figure 1's framework from pdf 181). pdf_page_range spans [181,183] to reflect this non-contiguous-but-conceptually-unified content, with SU-CP-10's page (182) falling inside that span but assigned to the separate receptor-pharmacology unit.

study_units.title: Drug-Receptor Interactions: Agonists and Antagonists
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Effects of Drugs on Receptors' heading confirmed on pdf page 182 (0182.json): agonists (affinity vs. efficacy, full vs. partial agonists, with named opioid-receptor examples methadone/morphine vs. buprenorphine) and antagonists (chemical, physiological/functional, and pharmacological -- competitive reversible/irreversible and non-competitive -- with named examples naloxone, phenoxybenzamine), illustrated by Figures 2-5 (log-dose-response curve shifts under each antagonism type, continuing onto pdf 183's Figure 6). Kept as its own unit distinct from SU-CP-09 because it tests a different skill (predicting a graph shift or clinical effect from a receptor-binding mechanism) than dose-response magnitude/safety-margin calculation.

study_units.title: Variability in Drug Response
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json declares CP.S02.T10's pdf_page_range as the whole CP.S02 section span (177-183, since TN TOC topic-level nodes are not independently page-anchored), but raw OCR of pdf page 184 (0184.json) shows the 'Variability in Drug Response' heading is actually printed at the TOP of pdf 184 -- immediately after Figure 6's caption (the last item confirmed on pdf 183) and immediately before the 'Therapeutic Drug Monitoring' heading, which is itself independently body-confirmed to start on pdf 184 per CP.S03's own extraction record. Per same-page-merge protocol step 4, the tighter body-confirmed single-page bound [184,184] is used in place of the TOC node's nominal section-wide declaration. Content: intake/absorption/distribution/biotransformation/elimination/PD-level causes of interindividual dosing variability -- framed here as context that motivates the TDM content immediately following it (SU-CP-12), rather than as its own testable clinical action.

study_units.title: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Therapeutic Drug Monitoring' heading confirmed on pdf page 184 (0184.json) via BODY_HEADING_CONFIRMATION (matching toc_inventory.json's own extraction_method for this node): definition, indications for TDM (low TI, unpredictable dose-response, high-stakes toxicity/failure, wide interpatient PK variability), role of nomograms, and the named low-TI drug list (vancomycin, aminoglycosides, digoxin, phenytoin/anticonvulsants, warfarin, lithium), plus a sidebar of tips to reduce drug-related adverse events in the elderly.

study_units.title: Drug Interactions (Mechanisms and Clinically Significant Examples)
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Drug Interactions' confirmed as its own bold sub-heading on pdf page 185 (0185.json), directly following 'Approach to Suspected Adverse Drug Reactions': PK-interaction mechanisms (absorption/distribution/metabolism/excretion changes) vs. PD-interaction mechanisms (additive/synergistic/antagonistic effects), plus an extensive sidebar table of named clinically-relevant interactions (warfarin + ciprofloxacin/macrolides/metronidazole/TMP-SMX, warfarin + acetaminophen, OCP + rifampin, sildenafil + nitrates, SSRIs + St. John's wort or MAOIs [serotonin syndrome], statins + niacin/fibrates/macrolides/azoles [rhabdomyolysis], TMP-SMX + ACEi/ARB/spironolactone [hyperkalemia]). Kept as its own unit separate from SU-CP-13 because the sidebar's named-interaction content is a distinct, high-yield testable surface in its own right rather than an extension of the ADR-classification/reporting workflow.

study_units.title: Autonomic Nervous System Physiology and Pharmacology
source_hierarchy_path: CP.S04 (Adverse Drug Reactions) [same-page merge resolution: Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology portion]
study_units.structural_rationale: Second resolved heading from the CP.S04 same-page merge (see SU-CP-13). 'Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology' confirmed as its own bold heading near the bottom of pdf page 185 (0185.json), with Figure 7 (subdivisions of the peripheral nervous system) and general ACh/NE neurotransmitter/receptor-termination content. Content continues onto pdf 186 (0186.json) with confirmed 'Parasympathetic Nervous System' (craniosacral origin, M1/M2 muscarinic receptors) and 'Sympathetic Nervous System' (thoracolumbar origin, paravertebral/prevertebral ganglia, beta1/beta2/alpha1/alpha2/M3 receptor distribution) sub-headings, plus Table 3 (direct autonomic-receptor effects on the cardiorespiratory system) and Figure 8. This unit represents only the ANS-physiology portion of the merge; the third TOC sub-entry under this heading, 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain', is thematically unrelated to autonomic physiology (an opioid-prescribing clinical guideline, not ANS content) despite being nested under this heading in the printed TOC layout, so it is kept as its own separate unit, SU-CP-16, rather than folded in here.

study_units.title: Opioid Therapy for Chronic Non-Cancer Pain
source_hierarchy_path: CP.S04.T05 (Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain)
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain' confirmed as its own bold heading near the bottom of pdf page 186 (0186.json) -- immediately following the Table-3/Figure-8 autonomic content, textually and thematically unconnected to it -- with 'General Management Principles' (optimize non-opioid therapy first; avoid high doses; restrict starting dose to <90 MME/day, ideally <50 MME/day; taper collaboratively for patients on >=90 MME/day), continuing onto pdf 187 (0187.json) with guidance on multidisciplinary tapering programs and a citation to the national (Canadian) opioid guideline (CMAJ 2017, also listed in the chapter's own References on pdf 188).

study_units.title: Common Drug Endings (Suffix-to-Class Recognition)
study_units.structural_rationale: 'Common Drug Endings' heading confirmed on pdf page 187 (0187.json), directly following the Opioid Therapy content: Table 4, a 17-row suffix-to-drug-class mapping (e.g., -olol -> beta-blocker, -pril -> ACE inhibitor, -sartan -> ARB, -statin -> HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, -mab -> monoclonal antibody, -caine -> local anesthetic), with a documented exception note (methimazole/itraconazole/nystatin do not follow the general -azole pattern).

study_units.structural_rationale: 'Dangerous Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations' heading confirmed on pdf page 187 (0187.json), directly following Table 4: Table 5, the ISMP Canada error-prone abbreviation/symbol/dose-designation list (e.g., 'U' for unit mistaken for zero/four, trailing-zero and lack-of-leading-zero decimal errors, QD/QOD confusion, ambiguous eye-laterality abbreviations) with each entry's intended meaning, the specific error risk, and the ISMP-recommended correction.

study_units.title: References / Bibliography
source_hierarchy_path: CP.S06 (Landmark Pharmacology Trials) [same-page merge resolution: References portion]

Raw OCR of body page 0188.json confirms 'References' as its own distinct heading immediately following the two landmark-trial summaries, opening with a full run-on bibliography of >30 alphabetically-ordered citations (e.g., ACOG Practice Bulletin on hormonal contraception; Boyer, 'The serotonin syndrome', NEJM 2005; Busse et al., opioid-therapy guideline, CMAJ 2017; multiple TMP-SMX/hyperkalemia case-control studies; Kalant/Grant/Mitchell, 'Principles of medical pharmacology'). No content was reattached elsewhere; there is nothing here beyond the citation list itself.
